title: [profiler][cupti] Turn kernel latency timestamps back off when nothing wants QUEUED
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.17.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #192370

The CUPTI monitor enables the per-subscriber
CUPTI_ACTIVITY_ATTR_ENABLE_KERNEL_LATENCY_TIMESTAMPS attribute the first time an
observer selects the QUEUED kernel field, and then never turns it off:
_latency_enabled was a one-way latch and enable_kernel_latency_timestamps was
only ever called with True. Unregistering the observer that asked for QUEUED
dropped the field from the enabled selection but left the attribute armed on the
subscription, so a session paid for latency timestamps for the rest of the
process -- exactly what the "so the always-on timing path pays no latency
overhead" comment was trying to avoid. In practice a ProfilerObserver registered
once leaves every later node-timer-only step running with the feature on.

Make it track the field selection like every other kind/field the monitor
reconciles: enabled iff some registered observer selects QUEUED, and disabled
again when the last one goes away. The call stays best-effort (the result is
ignored, as before) so a CUPTI that refuses the attribute just keeps its current
behaviour.

stop() has to forget the flag as well. It tears down the subscription, and the
attribute is a property of that subscription, so leaving _latency_enabled set
would make the next session see a stale "already enabled" and never arm it for
the new subscriber -- silently losing queued/submitted after any stop/start.

Found while investigating a CUDA driver hang whose precondition is latency
timestamps being enabled; this is not a fix for that hang.

Test Plan:
New regression test drives register -> register(QUEUED) -> unregister and asserts
the enable/disable calls and the flag:

```
python -m pytest test/profiler/test_cupti_monitor.py \
    -k 'latency_timestamps_track'
```

Passes with this change; without it the test fails at the unregister step
(enable calls are [True] rather than [True, False], and _latency_enabled stays
True). The tests covering the code paths this touches (activity normalization,
configure/singleton, external correlation, approx timestamps) also pass:

```
python -m pytest test/profiler/test_cupti_monitor.py \
    -k 'latency or normalize_activities or configure or singleton or external_correlation or approx'
```

Lint:

```
lintrunner -a torch/profiler/_cupti/monitor.py test/profiler/test_cupti_monitor.py
```

This commit was authored with the assistance of an AI coding agent.
